_comment: Units are SI: mass in kg, lengths in metres, torque in Nm, rpm as rpm.
weight_bias_front is the fraction of static mass over the front axle -
a front transverse layout sits near 0.62, a mid-engine near 0.42, and a
rear-engine 911 near 0.38. It is the single biggest handling character
knob, so it is worth getting roughly right per car.
grip_lat / grip_long are peak friction coefficients on tarmac with the
tires the car left the factory on. tarmac_grip / dirt_grip are compound
multipliers layered on top by the tire part fitted.
Adding a car needs no code: append an entry here.

cars.description: Slow, soft and indestructible. Free to repair, forever.
600 kilos of duroplast and two strokes. Astonishingly light.
Soft, tall and front-drive, with a dashboard gearchange. Slow enough to be forgiving.
Two cylinders behind the back axle. Nothing about it is fast except the way it changes direction.
Six hundred and eighty kilos with the engine behind the back axle. Lift mid-corner and find out.
Soft as a sofa and leans like a yacht, but it will not let go until long after anything else has.
Front-drive, nose-heavy, and it pulls straight out of hairpins.
Hydragas suspension and a square steering wheel. Rolls like a boat, grips better than it looks.
A licence-built saloon with a long boot and no interest in stopping.
Engine behind the rear axle. Lift mid-corner and find out.
A Renault 12 that never stopped being built. Utterly plain and hard to break.
Wheels at the corners and no overhang worth the name. Turns in like nothing else at this money.
Air-cooled and tail-heavy. Traction out of a muddy hairpin, terror at the end of a fast one.
Light, revvy and endlessly tunable. The obvious first project.
Genuinely rallied in period. The quickest thing in the starter fleet, and it knows it.
The one that actually won rallies. Front-drive, freewheeling, and happier on gravel than tarmac.
Seven hundred kilos. Not fast, but nothing else changes direction like it.
Cheap, light and eager. The obvious first upgrade out of the starter fleet.
A sixteen-valve engine in a car that weighs nothing. Needs revs and rewards them.
Small, stiff and eager. The cheapest way into a class where everyone is quick.
The one that started it. Light, revvy, and it will lift a rear wheel if you ask.
Fuel injection, a spoiler, and understeer you can lean on all day.
All the boost arrives at once and the inside front wheel gives up. Enormous fun.
The benchmark hot hatch. Nose-led, tidy, hard to upset.
Lift-off oversteer as a factory feature. Sharp, and it bites.
The high-revving answer to the Golf. Stronger top end, softer body.
A supercharged shopping car that revs to seven and a half. Absurd and reliable.
Revs to the moon and weighs nothing. Keep it above five thousand and it stays with far dearer cars.
Live rear axle, willing tail. The classroom for left-foot braking.
A brick with a turbocharger. Heavy, rear-drive, and it will sit sideways forever.
Not quick, perfectly balanced, and it tells you everything. The best classroom in the game.
A small turbo on a very light car. Nothing, nothing, then everything at once.
Not fast. Perfectly balanced. Rewards the driver, not the wallet.
Six cylinders, rear drive, and a limited-slip diff. Heavier than the hatches and far happier sideways.
Huge turbo, long wheelbase, rear drive. Boost arrives all at once.
Heavier than its rivals but planted, and it never runs out of grip early.
Flat-four low down, symmetrical AWD, endlessly forgiving on gravel.
Sharper and angrier than the Impreza. Less patient with mistakes.
Six championships of homologation. Points wherever you look.
The car that made four-wheel drive compulsory. Nose-heavy and stubborn.
440 Nm through the front wheels. The diff is doing heroic work.
Driver-adjustable centre diff. The setup sheet actually matters here.
Active yaw control in a homologation special. Turns in like nothing else.
A homologation car built in the modern era, for no reason but rallying.
Rear-biased AWD that only sends power forward when it has to.
Engine behind the rear axle. Traction out of corners, weight over the tail.
Two-metre wheelbase, mid-engine, no patience. Rotates on a thought.
Naturally aspirated V6. No lag at all, and it screams to nine thousand.
Mid-engine four-wheel drive in a supermini shell. Almost neutral.
Group B at its most absurd. Wait for the boost, then hold on.
Supercharged and turbocharged together, so there is no hole to fall into.
Purpose-built, composite-bodied, and the most powerful of the lot.
670 kilos, all suspension travel and no bodywork to bend.
Two and a half tonnes that lands jumps other cars would break on.
Heavy, brutal and impossible to unsettle. Point it and it goes.
700 horsepower, rear drive, rear engine. Tarmac only, if you value the car.
A raised, gravel-shod V10. Absurd, and genuinely quick off tarmac.
